newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria invites bidders for its chemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria invites bidders for its chemical plant.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Monday it has opened a new round for the sale of a 57 percent stake in the country's chemical fertiliser producer Chimko, stating a minimum price of $100.2 million.

"Last year, when the plant was offered for sale for the first time, we had only one candidate who offered less then $100 million and that's why now when we open a new round for bidding we set a minimum price," said a Privatisation Agency official, who declined to be named.

The Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov told the state radio that offers for the purchase of Chimko's stake would be accepted by July 9. "We have sent invitations to all strategic investors," he added.
Chimko officials said the plant's 1997 business plan, adopted by the directors board, had envisaged to finalise the deal within the first half of the year.

The plant imports 64 percent of its raw materials and exports 92 percent of its products. Its pre-tax revenue was 8.4 billion levs for the first 11 months of the year, plant officials said. They did not give further information.

From January until December the plant had produced some 717,000 tonnes of carbamide, 484,000 tonnes of ammonia, 12,000 tonnes of carbon sulphide and more than 2,500 cubic metres of argon, officials said.
They said Chimko has a 35.6 million lev gross profit for the first four months of the year. Annual net profit for this year is seen at some $20 million.
The Vratsa-based plant plans to produce this year 785,000 tonnes of carbamide, 525,000 tonnes of ammonia, 17,000 tonnes of carbon sulphide and 2.6 million cubic metres of argon.
Chimko has 20 installations, including for reforming, carbamide, carbon sulphide, carbon dioxide and a catalytic installation.
